title: Earlier leads, rechecked against all of California
question: Do the private providers the earlier drug and outlier screens named still stand out once they are set against all California billers in the full national drug file?
finding: Of 29 private provider numbers named by the earlier screens (Bay Area drug peers, or national service outliers), 5 are flagged again by at least one of the three new drug screens: PLANNED PARENTHOOD SHASTA DIABLO, INC. (product price or share); NORTH EAST MEDICAL SERVICES (one prescriber); WALGREEN CO (one prescriber); WALGREEN CO (one prescriber); MISSION AREA HEALTH ASSOCIATES, INC (against California peers). The others do not stand out against California peers in the drug file; for the service outliers that is expected, since their flags were for services, not drugs.
how: The national file (21,515,000 rows, one per billing number, prescribing number, drug code and month, 2018 to 2024) was read straight from the zip. 1,135,323 rows whose drug code is one digit repeated, a placeholder for a missing code, were dropped as the federal documentation advises: they carry a sum of $20,382.56 billion, which is not real money. A provider number counts as San Francisco when the California part of the national provider registry puts its practice address in San Francisco (252 billing numbers with drug money); California peers are all billing numbers in that registry file. A drug product is the first nine digits of the code (maker and product), package sizes added together; names come from Open Payments and Part D files that print a name beside a code. Earlier screens: the rows of `drug-spending` and `outliers` in the site’s “Medicaid billing” page that are outside City government and the University. Rank: the share of California peers with a lower payment per claim line in the biller’s largest year.
limits: Nothing here names or counts a patient; the file withholds small cells. The file mixes pharmacy claims with drugs given in clinics and amounts health plans report, does not drop denied claims, and counts claim lines, not quantities: a line for a 90-day supply or a high dose costs more without anything being wrong. Beneficiary-months add up each month’s count of people, so a person treated every month counts twelve times. A specialty pharmacy serving people with HIV, hepatitis or cancer, a hospital clinic, a fertility or eye practice will rightly stand far above an ordinary pharmacy. 2024 is preliminary. The registry places a provider by its address today. Not being flagged here does not clear a provider of the earlier pattern, which was measured differently.
